The '''Vermont Department of Corrections''' is the government agency in the [[U.S. state]] of [[Vermont]] charged with overseeing correctional facilities, supervising [[probation]] and [[parole]]es, and serving in an advisory capacity in the prevention of [[crime]] and [[juvenile delinquency]]. It is a part of the Vermont Agency of Human Services.<ref>[https://doc.vermont.gov/ State of Vermont website] accessed January 11, 2008</ref>

The agency is headquartered at the Waterbury State Office Complex in [[Waterbury, Vermont]].<ref>"[https://doc.vermont.gov/about/contact-us/ Contact the Vermont Department of Corrections] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200224154629/https://doc.vermont.gov/about/contact-us/ |date=2020-02-24 }}." Vermont Department of Corrections. Retrieved on February 24, 2020.</ref><ref>"[http://doc.vermont.gov/about/map/view Waterbury State Office Complex] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100825064732/http://doc.vermont.gov/about/map/view |date=2010-08-25 }}." Vermont Department of Corrections. Retrieved on February 24, 2020.</ref><ref>"[http://doc.vermont.gov/about About the Department of Corrections] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101027085953/http://doc.vermont.gov/about |date=2010-10-27 }}." Vermont Department of Corrections. Retrieved on February 24, 2020. "A map showing where the Department of Corrections Central Office is in the Waterbury State Office complex."</ref>

[[Nicholas J. Deml]] was appointed commissioner by [[Governor of Vermont|Vermont governor]] [[Phil Scott]] in November 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-10-09|title=Ex-CIA official to become Vermont corrections commissioner|url=https://apnews.com/article/congress-united-states-senate-cia-vermont-united-states-7b71161d840fb5a1011527d745f65ef5|access-date=2021-11-04|website=AP NEWS|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Keays|first=Alan J.|date=2021-10-08|title=Ex-CIA official, national security aide to head Vermont Department of commissioner Jim Baker, who served from December 2019 until October 2021.<ref>{{Cite ==State prison facilities==
As of 2018, the Vermont Department of Corrections manages the operations of six prison facilities in the state of Vermont. There were 1,422 prisoners in the system in October 2024.<ref>[http://doc.vermont.gov/about/reports/ff2007_adobe State of Vermont website] accessed January 11, 2008</ref>

Vermont's former Dale Women's Facility in [[Waterbury, Vermont]] closed in early 2009.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Corcoran|first1=Michael|title=Waterbury worries about closing Dale prison facility|url=http://www.stowetoday.com/stowereporter/archives/waterbury-worries-about-closing-dale-prison-facility/article_e7e0e92a-de6f-5aa6-94e8-dd7b8752f8e4.html|access-date=25 July 2016|publisher=Stowe Today|date=24 April 2008}}</ref>  State officials considered closing the Caledonia Community Work Camp (adjacent to the Northeast Regional Correctional Facility) in [[St. Johnsbury, Vermont|St. Johnsbury]] in March 2016 because of underpopulation.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Burbank|first1=April|title=Why Vermont could close St. Johnsbury prison work camp|url=http://www.burlingtonfreepress.com/story/news/politics/2016/03/13/why-vermont-could-close-st-johnsbury-prison-work-camp/81453576/|access-date=25 July 2016|newspaper=Burlington Free Press|date=14 March 2016}}</ref>

While security is handled by state employees, services, such as health services, have been contracted out.<ref>{{cite news | title=Editorial: Open government can't be privatized | url=http://www.burlingtonfreepress.com/article/20100902/OPINION01/9020303/Voice-of-the-Free-Press-Open-government-can-t-be-privatized| newspaper=Burlington Free Press | location=Burlington, Vermont | pages= 11A | date=2 September 2010 }}</ref>  There are 600 corrections officers.<ref>{{cite book |title = Local men graduate from corrections officer school | publisher = the Chronicle | date = September 12, 2007}}</ref>

The State of Vermont contracted with [[Corrections Corporation of America]] to house inmates in out-of-state private prisons beginning in the mid-1990s, and has continued the practice.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Krantz|first1=Laura|title=Vermont inmates on lockdown at Kentucky prison|url=http://vtdigger.wpengine.com/2014/01/21/vermont-inmates-lockdown-kentucky-prison/|access-date=29 July 2016|publisher=Vermont Digger|date=21 January 2014}}</ref>  About 115 prisoners are held outside the state of Vermont. These prisoners cost half as much as the prisoners in state because of the [[economies of scale]] in larger prisons, and because only healthy prisoners are exported.<ref name="chron080604">{{cite book | author = Gresser, Joseph |title = State outlines new prison policy | publisher = the Chronicle | date = June 4, 2008}}</ref>

In the past, the State of Vermont held prisoners at the [[Lee Adjustment Center]] in [[Beattyville, Kentucky]]<ref>{{cite news|last1=Davis|first1=Mark|title=Vermont Inmates Pine for Their Old Kentucky Prison|url=http://www.sevendaysvt.com/vermont/vermont-inmates-pine-for-their-old-kentucky-prison/Content?oid=3042079|access-date=29 July 2016|publisher=Seven Days|date=2 December 2015}}</ref>  (now closed), and at the [[Florence Correctional Center]] in [[Florence, Arizona]], both CCA properties. The State of Vermont also formally contracted with the [[GEO Group]] and transferred out-of-state prisoners to the [[North Lake Correctional Facility]] in Michigan.<ref>"[http://doc.vermont.gov/information-for-inmate-families-and-friends/inmates-housed-out-of-state/ Inmates Housed Out of State]." Vermont Department of Corrections. Retrieved on December 6, 2015.</ref>

The State of Vermont now contracts with [[CoreCivic]] to house inmates out of state at [[Tallahatchie County Correctional Facility]] in Mississippi.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Elder-Connors |first=Liam |date=2026-06-11 |title=Reporter’s notebook: Visiting Vermont prisoners in Mississippi |url=https://www.vermontpublic.org/local-news/2026-06-11/reporters-notebook-visiting-vermont-prisoners-mississippi |access-date=2026-08-24 |website=Vermont Public |language=en}}</ref>

==Probation and parole offices==

There are 13 community-based probation and parole offices throughout the state of Vermont. These are under the administrative jurisdiction of the Vermont Department of Corrections. The offices are located in Barre, Bennington, Brattleboro, Burlington, Chelsea (sub-office in Hartford District), Hartford, Middlebury (sub-office to Rutland), Morrisville, Newport, Rutland, St. Albans, St. Johnsbury, and Springfield.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://doc.vermont.gov/custody-supervision/field|title=Probation and Parole Offices — Department of Corrections|website=doc.vermont.gov/|access-date=2020-02-24|archive-date=2020-02-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200224154634/https://doc.vermont.gov/custody-supervision/field|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Fallen officers==
Since the establishment of the Vermont Department of Corrections, three officers have died in the line of duty.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.odmp.org/agency/4013-vermont-department-of-corrections-vermont|title=Vermont Department of Corrections, VT|website=The Officer Down Memorial Page (ODMP)}}</ref>
